advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test that drives `_as_backend_http_error` (and/or `_with_connection_retry` with a monkeypatched non-empty `_jira_http_error_types`) so a JIRAError-shaped error with `.status_code` is verified to become a `BackendHTTPError` with matching `.code`.
evidence: `_dc_error` builds the neutral type directly: `from rebar_reconciler._backend import BackendHTTPError ... return BackendHTTPError(...)` (test file lines 34-44) — the transport's translation is never invoked
transport.py:219-220 `except http_errors as exc:` / `raise _as_backend_http_error(exc) from exc` is the code under review and is not driven by any assertion here
transport.py:138-142 `_jira_http_error_types` returns `()` when `from jira.exceptions import JIRAError` raises ImportError
resolve_symbol: `JIRAError` in `jira.exceptions` is UNRESOLVED (not importable) — so under unit tests `http_errors == ()` and the translation branch is dead

Existing unit test asserts the untranslated behavior: `with pytest.raises(FakeHttpError): ... get_issue('DC-1')` (test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py:178-179), confirming translation does not run without the real library
The live coverage is gated: `@_skip` / `@_skip_no_extra` on the DC transport exception tests (tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py:284-285)
advisory.finding: The new transport translation seam — `_as_backend_http_error` (status_code->code) and the `except http_errors as exc: raise _as_backend_http_error(exc)` choke point in `_with_connection_retry` — has no gating test. The new heldout test constructs `BackendHTTPError` by hand (`_dc_error`) and only feeds it to the CORE functions; it never verifies the DC transport translates a library JIRAError into `BackendHTTPError`. Because `jira` is not installed in the unit/CI environment, `_jira_http_error_types()` returns `()`, making the `except http_errors` branch and `_as_backend_http_error` unreachable in the unit tier; the only tier that would exercise them is skip-gated live tests. The core translation logic this diff adds could be entirely broken (wrong attribute, wrong urllib arg order, not caught) and every test in the new file plus CI would still pass.
scenarios: A regression renames the read attribute (e.g. reads `.code` instead of `.status_code`) or swaps urllib's `(url, code, msg, hdrs, fp)` arg order — every heldout assertion still passes because it never exercises `_as_backend_http_error`
The `except http_errors` clause is removed or reordered so a JIRAError escapes untranslated — unit tests stay green because `http_errors` is empty without the extra
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches `transport._jira_http_error_types` to return a fake exception type carrying `.status_code`, raises it through `_with_connection_retry`, and asserts `pytest.raises(BackendHTTPError)` with `exc.code == status`; plus a direct call to `_as_backend_http_error(FakeHttpError(404))` asserting `.code == 404`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `_as_backend_http_error` maps an exception with a missing or non-int `.status_code` to `.code == 0`.
evidence: transport.py:156-159 `status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)` / `int(status) if isinstance(status, int) else 0`

No test in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler constructs a JIRAError-shaped error with an absent/non-int status_code (search for `status_code` in the new file only hits `_dc_error(404).code == 404`, a pre-set int)
ABSENCE: the branch is stated as a deliberate safety contract in the docstring but has no exercising assertion
advisory.finding: The `_as_backend_http_error` degrade-to-0 edge is untested: `int(status) if isinstance(status, int) else 0` covers a missing or non-int `.status_code`, a path the docstring calls out ('A library error with no usable status degrades to 0, which no core branch mistakes for a 404/success'), yet no test injects a library error lacking a usable status.
scenarios: A DC JIRAError with `status_code=None` (or a string) — the else branch must yield 0; if it instead threw or produced a spurious 404, deletion detection would misfire, and no test would catch it

coaching.coaching: Add a regression test covering the degrade-to-0 path for missing or non-int status_code.
